monthly_review.summary: You've shifted toward faster, more intense running this month with higher average HR and pace, but at the cost of reduced aerobic volume and efficiency. Your zone distribution shows a notable increase in Z3–Z4 work.
monthly_review.highlight: Your Z3–Z4 time increased from 22% to 46% of total HR zone distribution — nearly double last month’s intensity exposure, while Z1–Z2 dropped from 79% to 51%.

goal_tracker.message: You need 19.3 more km across 4 sessions in the remaining 17 days — averaging 4.8 km/session — to match last month’s distance. Given your recent 11.1 km long run and ability to sustain 162 spm at 3.0 km, 2–3 runs of 5–6 km (including one Zone 2 endurance run) will close the gap.

insights.title: Efficiency improved despite lower volume
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency rose from 13.42 to 13.95 km/hr per bpm — driven by faster paces (+43 sec/km improvement) and higher cadence (+6 spm), even as total volume dropped. This suggests better neuromuscular coordination under load.

insights.title: Sharp shift toward threshold and VO2 max work
insights.body: Z3–Z4 time jumped from 22% (last month) to 46% (this month), while Z1–Z2 collapsed from 79% to 51%. Notably, your 3.0 km run on 2026-06-11 hit 144 bpm and 162 spm — solidly in upper Z3 — indicating readiness for structured threshold work, but insufficient Z2 base support.

insights.title: Cadence-stride tradeoff emerging
insights.body: Cadence increased +6 spm (146 → 152), yet stride length remained low (69–71 cm on easy/long runs vs 91–95 cm during hard efforts). Ground contact time dropped from 314 ms (11.1 km) to 274 ms (3.0 km), confirming form sharpening at speed — but may reflect fatigue or lack of Z2 consistency to reinforce economy at sub-threshold paces.

insights.title: High-intensity density without recovery buffer
insights.body: Four of your five recent runs (including two on same day, 2026-06-04) were ≥2.6 aerobic TE — three exceeded 3.0. Yet your longest run (11.1 km) was only 9.28 min/km (508 sec/km), well below your best pace (392 sec/km = 6:32 min/km), suggesting accumulated fatigue limited true quality execution.

recommendations.action: Do a 6.0 km Zone 2 run tomorrow (HR <138 bpm, pace ~9:30–10:00 min/km) with cadence consciously held at 148–150 spm and ground contact >310 ms
recommendations.reason: Your Z1–Z2 volume dropped 28% MoM; this rebuilds aerobic base while reinforcing efficient stride mechanics observed in your 11.1 km run (314 ms GCT, 69.7 cm stride)

recommendations.action: Replace one upcoming short run with a 12-min progressive surge: 4 min Z2 (135–139 bpm), 4 min Z3 (148–153 bpm), 4 min Z4 (158–163 bpm), all at consistent 155–158 spm
recommendations.reason: Your Z4 time is up to 22% but lacks specificity — this bridges Z3–Z4 with controlled cadence and HR targeting your observed Z4 threshold (159 bpm in 1.0 km effort on 2026-06-04)

recommendations.action: After your next run, perform 3 × 60-sec single-leg balance holds (eyes open → eyes closed) on each leg, tracking vertical oscillation trend over next 3 runs
recommendations.reason: Vertical oscillation increased from 7.6–7.7 cm (easy/long runs) to 8.4–9.2 cm (hard efforts); stability work may help dampen excess bounce without sacrificing stride length

weekly_focus.description: Re-establish Z2 as the metabolic and mechanical foundation — using heart rate discipline to restore efficiency, reduce vertical oscillation drift, and create margin for future intensity.
suggested_sessions: 45-min easy run with cadence focus (148–152 spm, GCT >310 ms)
